2608.26849.title: LiveSim: Simulating Environment-Shaped Users in Multi-Agent Live-Stream Ecosystems
2608.26849.paper_summary: User behavior simulation with large language models~(LLMs) is increasingly used to support multi-agent ecosystem simulation. Existing simulators typically rely on static user profiles inferred from historical observations, which become inadequate in socially intensive environments such as live streaming where interaction dynamics continuously reshape user behavior. We propose \textbf{LiveSim}, an LLM-based framework for live-stream ecosystem simulation. It represents users as editable behavioral hypotheses and progressively refines them through trajectory-grounded interactions, where discrepancies between simulated and observed trajectories reveal missing environmental shaping effects. These signals are further extracted as transferable environment-behavior patterns and accumulated in a collective behavioral memory to improve user-level behavioral fidelity and support ecosystem-level simulation. Experiments on real-world live-stream risk-control data validate the effectiveness of LiveSim in improving user-level behavioral fidelity and enabling ecosystem-level analysis of risk evolution and platform intervention effects.
2608.26849.paper_summary_zh: 用大型語言模型（LLMs）進行用戶行為模擬越來越多地被用來支持多代理生態系統模擬。現有的模擬器通常依賴於從歷史觀察中推斷的靜態用戶檔案，但在社交密集的環境中，如直播，這些檔案變得不足，因為互動動態不斷重塑用戶行為。我們提出了\textbf{LiveSim}，這是一個基於LLM的直播生態系統模擬框架。它將用戶表示為可編輯的行為假設，並通過基於軌跡的互動逐步細化這些假設，其中模擬和觀察到的軌跡之間的差異揭示了缺失的環境塑造效應。這些信號進一步被提取為可轉移的環境-行為模式，並累積在集體行為記憶中，以提高用戶層級的行為真實性並支持生態系統層級的模擬。對現實世界直播風險控制數據的實驗驗證了LiveSim在提高用戶層級行為真實性和實現生態系統層級風險演變及平台干預效果分析方面的有效性。
